title: Adult cardiac arrest and post-ROSC care

sources.title: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and ECC (AHA; Wigginton JG, et al. Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
Adult Cardiac Arrest Algorithm (AHA 2025 Guidelines for CPR and ECC)
Part 11: Post-Cardiac Arrest Care: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and ECC (AHA; doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001375)
Adult Post-Cardiac Arrest Care Algorithm (AHA 2025 Guidelines for CPR and ECC)
Cardiac Arrest in Pregnancy In-Hospital ACLS Algorithm (AHA 2025 Guidelines for CPR and ECC)

q_rhythm.text: Arrest called, CPR running, pads on. What does the monitor show at this rhythm check?

q_shocks.text: Shockable rhythm. How many shocks already given?

q_ste.text: ROSC. Post-ROSC 12-lead ECG: persistent ST elevation?

q_unstable.text: Cardiogenic shock or recurrent VT/VF after ROSC?

q_commands.text: Follows commands (off sedation and paralysis, if able to assess)?

e_first_shock.title: VF/pVT: first shock
actions: Shock once, then resume CPR immediately for 2 minutes.
Biphasic energy: per manufacturer (e.g. 120-200 J); if unknown, use the maximum. Monophasic: 360 J.
High-quality CPR: rate 100-120/min, depth at least 5 cm, full recoil, minimal pauses.
Get IV access (IO if IV fails). No drugs yet in this cycle.
Waveform capnography; consider an advanced airway.
Recheck rhythm after 2 minutes and re-enter this pathway.
cautions: Single shocks, not stacked.
Change compressor every 2 minutes or sooner if tired.

If pregnant with fundal height at or above the umbilicus (AHA 2025 pregnancy algorithm): continuous left lateral uterine displacement; IV above the diaphragm; detach fetal monitors; early airway by the most experienced person (difficult airway common); if on IV magnesium, stop it and give calcium (dose per local protocol); call the maternal arrest team; aim for resuscitative delivery by 5 minutes if no ROSC, depending on local resources.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_refractory_vf.title: Refractory VF/pVT (3 or more shocks)
actions: Continue shocks with 2 minutes of CPR between rhythm checks.
Defibrillate at the same or higher energy than the first shock (AHA 2025: later shocks equivalent; higher may be considered).
Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO every 3-5 minutes.
Amiodarone IV/IO (fixed dose, not weight-based): first dose 300 mg; ONE second dose of 150 mg; no further amiodarone boluses (the AHA 2025 algorithm lists only these two doses).
Or lidocaine IV/IO (weight-based): first dose 1-1.5 mg/kg; then 0.5-0.75 mg/kg; maximum total dose per local protocol.
Track antiarrhythmic doses already given: this screen is re-entered at every 2-minute check.
Actively treat causes: coronary occlusion, PE, hypo/hyperkalaemia, toxins, tension pneumothorax, tamponade.
Check CPR quality on capnography: aim for ETCO2 of at least 10, ideally 20 mmHg or more.
Senior decision on ECPR or transfer if locally available.
cautions: Vector change or double sequential defibrillation after 3 or more shocks: usefulness not established (AHA 2025).
ECPR was not covered in the guideline pages reviewed: local programme decision.

If pregnant with fundal height at or above the umbilicus (AHA 2025 pregnancy algorithm): continuous left lateral uterine displacement; IV above the diaphragm; detach fetal monitors; early airway by the most experienced person (difficult airway common); if on IV magnesium, stop it and give calcium (dose per local protocol); call the maternal arrest team; aim for resuscitative delivery by 5 minutes if no ROSC, depending on local resources.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_nonshock.title: Asystole / PEA
actions: CPR for 2 minutes between rhythm checks.
Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO as soon as feasible, then every 3-5 minutes.
IV first; IO if IV fails. Waveform capnography; consider an advanced airway.
Treat reversible causes: hypovolaemia, hypoxia, acidosis, hypo/hyperkalaemia, hypothermia, tension pneumothorax, tamponade, toxins, pulmonary or coronary thrombosis.
If the rhythm becomes shockable, go to the VF/pVT branch.
cautions: POCUS may help find causes but must not lengthen pauses in compressions.
Calcium or bicarbonate only for a specific indication (e.g. hyperkalaemia, toxin) per local protocol, not routinely.
Termination in an intubated patient: ETCO2 below 10 mmHg after 20 minutes of ALS is one factor only; use no single ETCO2 cutoff if not intubated.

If pregnant with fundal height at or above the umbilicus (AHA 2025 pregnancy algorithm): continuous left lateral uterine displacement; IV above the diaphragm; detach fetal monitors; early airway by the most experienced person (difficult airway common); if on IV magnesium, stop it and give calcium (dose per local protocol); call the maternal arrest team; aim for resuscitative delivery by 5 minutes if no ROSC, depending on local resources.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_cath_now.title: ROSC with ST elevation
actions: Emergency coronary angiography, regardless of coma.
Oxygen: 100% until SpO2 or PaO2 is reliable, then SpO2 90-98%.
PaCO2 35-45 mmHg unless severe acidaemia.
MAP at least 65 mmHg with fluid and/or vasopressor.
If not following commands: start temperature control (see the comatose result).
cautions: If no cath lab on site: urgent transfer per local STEMI network.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_cath_consider.title: ROSC with shock or electrical instability
actions: Emergency coronary angiography is reasonable even without ST elevation.
Consider mechanical circulatory support with cardiology.
Oxygen to SpO2 90-98% once reliable; PaCO2 35-45 mmHg; MAP at least 65 mmHg.
If shock persists, go to the pathway: Cardiogenic shock.
cautions: Treat recurrent VT/VF using the pathway Tachycardia with a pulse (adult), or this pathway if pulseless, while arranging angiography.

MAP targets differ by source: AHA 2025 post-arrest care says MAP at least 65 mmHg; the Cardiogenic shock pathway uses above 60-65 mmHg (ACC 2025 cardiogenic shock guidance). A MAP of 65 or more meets both; the ranges come from different guidelines, not a contradiction.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_comatose.title: Post-ROSC, not following commands
actions: Start deliberate temperature control, goal 32-37.5 C, as soon as possible, for at least 36 hours.
Avoid rewarming faster than 0.5 C per hour.
SpO2 90-98% once reliable; PaCO2 35-45 mmHg; MAP at least 65 mmHg.
Glucose: avoid below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) and above 180 mg/dL (10 mmol/L).
EEG; treat clinical and non-convulsive seizures.
Consider CT (head, chest, abdomen, pelvis) and/or POCUS or echo to find the cause.
cautions: No routine seizure prophylaxis.
Delay prognosis: multimodal assessment at least 72 hours after normothermia and stopping sedation.
Emergency angiography without ST elevation, shock or electrical instability is not better than a delayed or selective approach.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_awake.title: Post-ROSC, following commands
actions: SpO2 90-98%; PaCO2 35-45 mmHg; MAP at least 65 mmHg.
Glucose 70-180 mg/dL (3.9-10 mmol/L).
Find and treat the cause of arrest.
Coronary angiography before discharge if a cardiac cause is suspected.
cautions: Recheck for deterioration; repeat this branch if mental state worsens.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_epi.title: VF/pVT after 1 shock: second shock and epinephrine
actions: Shock again, then CPR for 2 minutes.
Defibrillate at the same or higher energy than the first shock (AHA 2025: later shocks equivalent; higher may be considered).
Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO during this cycle, then every 3-5 minutes.
Consider an advanced airway with waveform capnography.
Recheck rhythm after 2 minutes and re-enter this pathway.
cautions: Vasopressin does not add benefit over epinephrine alone; high-dose epinephrine is not recommended.

If pregnant with fundal height at or above the umbilicus (AHA 2025 pregnancy algorithm): continuous left lateral uterine displacement; IV above the diaphragm; detach fetal monitors; early airway by the most experienced person (difficult airway common); if on IV magnesium, stop it and give calcium (dose per local protocol); call the maternal arrest team; aim for resuscitative delivery by 5 minutes if no ROSC, depending on local resources.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_antiarrhythmic.title: VF/pVT after 2 shocks: third shock and antiarrhythmic
actions: Shock again, then CPR for 2 minutes.
Defibrillate at the same or higher energy than the first shock (AHA 2025: later shocks equivalent; higher may be considered).
Amiodarone IV/IO (fixed dose, not weight-based): first dose 300 mg; ONE second dose of 150 mg later if VF/pVT persists; no further boluses.
Or lidocaine IV/IO (weight-based): first dose 1-1.5 mg/kg; then 0.5-0.75 mg/kg; maximum total dose per local protocol.
Continue epinephrine 1 mg every 3-5 minutes.
Treat reversible causes: hypovolaemia, hypoxia, acidosis, hypo/hyperkalaemia, hypothermia, tension pneumothorax, tamponade, toxins, pulmonary or coronary thrombosis.
Recheck rhythm every 2 minutes.
cautions: Routine calcium and sodium bicarbonate are not recommended.

If pregnant with fundal height at or above the umbilicus (AHA 2025 pregnancy algorithm): continuous left lateral uterine displacement; IV above the diaphragm; detach fetal monitors; early airway by the most experienced person (difficult airway common); if on IV magnesium, stop it and give calcium (dose per local protocol); call the maternal arrest team; aim for resuscitative delivery by 5 minutes if no ROSC, depending on local resources.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.
